Once upon a time, three little pigs set off to build homes of their own.
Pip liked to do things quickly.
Poppy liked to make things beautiful.
And Bruno liked to think things through.
They found three sunny spots beside a winding woodland path. Neighbors! said Poppy. Perfect, said Bruno.
Whoever finishes first gets a nap! said Pip. And off they went.
Pip gathered great armfuls of straw. He stacked it here. He tucked it there.
He pushed a door into the front. By lunchtime, he had a house. Finished!
A little piece of the roof drifted down onto his nose. Pip blew it away. Mostly finished.
He went inside, put his feet up, and fell asleep.
Poppy gathered sticks. Long sticks. Short sticks. Sticks with interesting little bends.
She tied them together, added a roof, and hung a flower beside the door.
Then she stepped back to admire her work. Lovely!
The house leaned a little to the left. Poppy straightened the flower. There. Much better.
Bruno built with bricks. He measured. He spread mortar. He laid each brick carefully.
One row. Then another. Then another.
Pip wandered over. Are you still building? Yes, said Bruno.
Poppy peeked around the wall. Would you like a flower? When I have somewhere to hang it.
By sunset, Bruno had finished a sturdy little house with a strong door, a snug roof, and a tall brick chimney.
He hung Poppy's flower beside the door. Then he sat down. Now, he said, I'm ready for that nap.
But someone else had just woken up. Someone with sharp ears. A long nose. And a very empty stomach.
The wolf came padding along the woodland path. He sniffed. He stopped. He smiled. Pig.
He followed his nose to Pip's straw house and knocked three times.
Little pig, little pig, let me come in!
Pip peered through a gap in the wall. He saw a nose. Then teeth. Rather a lot of teeth.
Not by the hair on my chinny chin chin!
The wolf straightened his shoulders. Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in!
He took a deep breath. He huffed. He puffed. And...
Pip shot out the back and raced down the path. Poppy! Open the door!
Poppy pulled him inside. What happened?
My house, panted Pip, has become a field.
Soon, three knocks rattled Poppy's door.
Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!
The pigs squeezed together behind the door. Not by the hairs on our chinny chin chins!
Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in!
The wolf took an even deeper breath. He huffed. He puffed.
The flower trembled. The walls rattled. And... down came the stick house!
Pip and Poppy scrambled out the back and ran straight to Bruno's. Open up!
Bruno opened the door. The pigs tumbled inside. Bruno shut it and slid the bolt.
For a moment, nobody spoke. Then Poppy held up one slightly crumpled flower. I saved this.
The wolf arrived at the brick house. He looked at the walls. He looked at the roof.
Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!
All three pigs answered together. Not by the hairs on our chinny chin chins!
Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in!
He planted his feet. He filled his chest. He huffed. He puffed. And...
Inside, Pip opened one eye. Are we still a house? We're still a house, said Bruno.
The wolf tried again. His cheeks bulged. His ears quivered.
He blew until he had to sit down. One small leaf landed on his head. The house stood firm.
Then the wolf looked up. The chimney.
Inside, the pigs heard footsteps on the roof. Pip pointed upward. Poppy looked toward the fireplace.
Bruno looked at the big tub of cold water beside his washing.
The three pigs looked at one another. Then they got to work.
Together, they pushed the tub into the empty fireplace.
Above them, the wolf squeezed into the chimney. Just a little farther, he muttered.
His feet slipped. His eyes widened. And down he came.
For one quiet moment, only his ears showed above the tub.
Then up popped a very wet wolf. Cold!
He scrambled out, dripping from nose to tail.
The pigs stood safely behind the kitchen table while Bruno pulled the cord that lifted the door latch.
The door swung open. The wolf needed no invitation.
He dashed outside and disappeared down the woodland path. This time, the huffing and puffing came from running.
The next morning, the three pigs got to work again. They built two more sturdy brick houses.
Pip carried bricks. Poppy measured walls. Bruno showed them how to spread the mortar.
And when the houses were finished, Poppy decorated every doorway.
That evening, the three pigs sat down together for supper.
Three spoons stopped halfway to three mouths. Bruno peeked through the window.
Then he smiled. It's only Rabbit.
Rabbit held up a basket. I brought buns.
Pip opened the door. Poppy put out another plate. And Bruno made room at the table.
Outside, the wind rustled the trees. Inside, the houses stayed sturdy, the buns stayed warm...
And nobody had to run anywhere. The end.
